Anyone else starting to multitask more to help their senior parent?

My mom is in her late 80s with mobility issues (uses a cane/walker) but is still incredibly sharp. Today I did yardwork (eg, mowing the lawn) *and then* groceries, which I rarely do, Anyone who has done yardwork knows there's nothing left in the tank, yet I still managed to squeeze a trip to the supermarket

Any advice to help my dad learn to sell things instead of buy more?

My dad is 69 and mom is 66. Money is not an issue. My mom is trying to downsize but my dad is defiant when it comes to getting rid of his stuff. They have a pretty big house that's just loaded with stuff and a very large garage that is quite full as well. It's not an episode of hoarders thankfully.

The problem is my dad says he knows he needs to downsize, but he can so easily buy things and can't let them go. He thinks everything he has is top end and high quality and can't be parted with unless absolute top dollar is gotten for it.

My mom is always trying to sell things or give them away and my dad can't let go of anything. Every single item is an argument. Every single one.

I live with them and finally blew up at my dad today. He asked me why I cared so much that he bought more speakers. He has an insane amount of stereo equipment already. I just told him he's leaving all this shit for me to have to deal with and he obviously doesn't care. Stuff that sits around in storage for years and is not used.

I just need to know if anyone else has had to deal with this and had success. A parent that just keeps buying things and has such a hard time selling them.

Money isn't a problem and there is no dementia or concerns with heath really, other than just general aging.

I am at my wits end and ready to just move away from them again, but I'd feel bad that I'd be leaving my mom to be the only person trying to overcome this massive backlog of "stuff".

Is long term memory loss normal?

My mum is 59 now and the last few years I noticed she starts to forget long term memories and replaces it with another false memory. I don’t know if it’s circumstance or age. 

She married an abusive man when I was 3 (she was 30) and they divorced when I was 19 (she was 46). I never noticed her having trouble with her memory until then. After that it was little things, not really noticeable (I don’t really remember well to give a specific example) so I just put it down to PTSD maybe a bit of dissociative amnesia. 

Then she remarried to a nice man a few years ago but that’s when I noticed it. For example, she always voted for one political party whilst I was growing up, but when she remarried she voted a different party which her new husband votes for and she insisted that she had always voted for that party, yet me and my siblings know she never did. We laughed about it because we thought it was weird but moved on. 

But lately it’s happening more and more and I’m a bit worried. For example, growing up she always told me her dad died of lung cancer. I very specifically remember her mentioning multiple times “it was weird because he never smoked”. Yet the other day we were talking about cancer and she told me her dad died of stomach cancer. I told her she had never said that and that it was lung cancer, and that her memory was being weird again. I dropped it in the end because recently we got into an argument when I last stayed with her about another memory (she confused a memory of my brother for me) and I was so frustrated trying to get my point across to her with her bad memories, she got really upset and since then I realised this is going on and that I should probably just let it go.

But I’m not sure if this is normal for her age or something to worry about?

Questions being new to this sub and upcoming phases with my parents

I discovered this sub in the last couple of days and have read through several threads here. My heart goes out to so many of you. To say it’s been eye opening and heart breaking is an understatement. I feel like I’m in some state of shock reading through these threads.

Similar in a way to personal finance, it seems like elder care is something everybody should be considering but education and awareness is tragically not prevalent. I think that’s a reason for my shock: how woefully uneducated I was before I found this sub, ignorantly assuming  ample options would be provided by waving the magic wand of Medicare, by my parents frequently telling me “everything is ok” when reviewing their documents and accounts they’re clearly not prepared, and now I’m low level freaking out about what lies ahead with my parents.

I have some questions that may come off sounding callous and very ignorant, but the actual intention is from a point of naive curiosity. I might even come off insensitive with my questions below even though that’s truly not my intention. If these premises aren’t convincing, I’m truly sorry and I’ll strive to be more sensitive in the future.

Many of the more gut wrenching stories I’ve read here are those whose parents weren’t unconditionally loving when their kids were younger, but the adult kids have stepped up to the plate being better people than their parents by acting as caretakers, providing time, care, and even money to help their parents.

And so many of these posts are from people who seem like, absent of being their parents caretakers, they aren’t exactly well enough financially to begin with, juggling their career, multiple jobs, raising kids and struggling to maintain their own relationships. Furthermore, many experience severe setbacks in careers, personal finances (going broke or in debt even! Sigh), to provide care themselves but also pay for services providing care to parents.

Many of you who do this are driven by guilt, which is understandable, and to potentially reduce regret in the future. Unconditional compassion is understandable too.

Are there other reasons that I’m missing for stepping up to care for parents who had fallen short when they were raising their kids when they were young? Are there legal obligations? Cultural ones I’m not aware of?

Next point might be out of line for me to ask, but I’m assuming in many instances, the economy was more favorable for parents to invest and build up savings etc than the economy and career prospects have been for the kids of those same parents. I’m assuming one acceptable path of aging care is for the parents savings and assets to be exhausted before the kids jump in. But what if the kids don’t or can’t?

Fortunately I have some funds and some flexibility in my schedule in this phase of my life.

But I can’t even begin to imagine how those who aren’t as lucky as I am feel. I just feel that for those of you in this sub, I’m at a loss for words- I feel incredulous and my heart drops through the floor for you. But I’m curious to those family caretakers, what causes you to do what you do?

Possible for health insurance denial if they deem someone unfit to live semi-independently?

My father recently had a bad fall that led to a stint in the ICU. He lives at his home alone, with a friend stopping by to help him with things. He uses a walker, and has some cognitive impairments from alcohol abuse and a mild stroke. This living situation obviously isn’t ideal, but he will not agree to assisted living at this time. His insurance company (UHC Advantage plan) asked me a few questions about his current living situation, and what we have planned after his release. I said assisted living would be the best choice for him, but he may refuse. Also, insurance does know that part of his recent hospitalization was due to alcohol withdrawal, so of course that is adding to the risk of him being alone and falling again.

If he goes back to living semi-independently, are they able to deem that situation unsafe, and deny a future claim if he falls again or anything like that? We are worried we won’t be able to get him to agree to an assisted living or long term care facility and this same thing could happen again. Can the insurance company deny a claim for this?

no longer caregiving

back in may my partner broke up with me, we have been no contact since near the end of july. i used to be her caregiver as she has an array of physical and mental conditions/disabilities that impact her daily life. 

something that is now impacting my daily life is the stress and guilt i face knowing that i am no longer there to look after her as she has struggled especially at night. since no contact, i have been worrying immensely about any flare ups or pain she will go through. i was the only person that took care of her as her family does not give her any support. before we went no contact i suggested to her that we look into getting her a professional caregiver to help her but she outrightly refused to do so as she did not want anyone but me to be her caregiver despite her conditions getting progressively worse. 

it’s been extraordinarily difficult since she split up with me because besides from grieving from heartbreak, i can’t stop worrying about her being in pain and i can’t be there to do something about it. it takes everything in me every day not to break no contact because i’m just so genuinely fearful of something awful or life threatening happening to her. i am aware it is no longer my responsibility to worry and care for her anymore especially now that we have no contact, but it has not made this anxiety go away or any easier to deal with.

if anyone has any advice on how to cope with this it would be much appreciated, i couldn’t find much info online in regard to something like this.

Turning Dad over in bed - lateral turn for bedbound

My dad has pretty advanced Parkinsons. He is a big guy - around 280lbs, and my mom is is his primary caregiver. He's been in a rehab hospital following a fall, and now he and my mom want to bring him home (yes I know a facility would be a good idea - they don't want to do that). They cannot afford a full-time caregiver. He had an evaluation from Hospice and they said he's not quite ready yet. Home health will be coming but they are not there 24-7. My dad is completely incontinent. We have gotten a purewick for the urine, but the primary obstacle for my mom is turning him over to clean up poo. He's big and she has zero muscles (and he doesn't/can't help much). So far I've found two possible items to help: 

A. A hoyer lift can be used to turn someone on their side in bed (a lateral turn). If anyone else is interested, here are a few videos of how its done. I haven't tried it myself yet. 

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6Q8nbxpNyE](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6Q8nbxpNyE)

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rf0i4jDn96M](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rf0i4jDn96M)

B. I found this device - the Q2 Roller - lateral turning device, which is designed for single-caregiver use. However, its being marketed to hospitals and as such is only being sold in packs of 5. I would buy one for $400, but not 5 for $2000. 

[https://www.reosmedical.com/products/q2roller](https://www.reosmedical.com/products/q2roller)

My questions for you all: 

1. Has anyone used one of these methods of turning at home? If so, how well did it work. 

2. Does anyone know where I could purchase an individual Q2 Roller? 

3. Are there any other mechanical means of turning a bed-bound person? 

Thanks!

Has caregiving made your senses hyper-sensitive?

I am currently taking care of my 77-year-old mother who has had spinal stenosis for over three years. A good way to describe it is imagining someone with ALS that progresses to about 50% and just stops and no more serious damage is done. She has less control of her body than her mother did at age 90.

So, I am living with her right now and find myself auditorily hyper-sensitive. If she is watching TV and someone yells on it, I will go to where she is to make sure it was not her. She has a phone and can page me with it, but I have to consider that she may not be able to get to her phone or perhaps I forget to charge mine. Stuff like that.

What do you do when you're constantly worried about your parents living alone?

My mom is in her 70s and still fairly independent, but I’ve been feeling constantly on edge lately. Every time she doesn’t answer my message right away, my mind starts spiraling - “what if she fell?”, “what if she forgot to lock the door?”, or just… anything. I knew I couldn't hover over her forever, so after a lot of internal debate, I got her this small alert device from a company called BeWell. It’s pretty simple - if something happens (like a fall), or if she presses the button, I get a message. It doesn’t solve everything, but it gave me a bit of peace. Honestly, I hadn’t slept through the night in weeks before that. 

Just wondering - has anyone else tried something similar? Or how do you personally manage that kind of worry without driving yourself crazy?

Wound Care

Has anyone else ever had issues where it seems like going to a wound care clinic just makes it worse?

My dad has diabetes and developed a blister on the bottom of his foot. We almost had it completely healed, but the doctor sent him to visit a wound care clinic periodically to get the dead skin removed and make sure it healed up. Ever since he started going to these appointments, his blister has just gotten worse and worse. He even has to take antibiotics now because of how much worse it's gotten. It's incredibly frustrating, and we are worried it's just going to get worse. Has anyone else had similar issues with wound care making things worse? Did they make it worse, or did they just uncover a hidden issue?

My watch is over

and my heart hurts, literally aches, right now. But I am relieved. At the end, she was not really living. She died in my arms here at home 24 hours ago and it's like my entire cellular structure is reminding me of her last moments. I just opened the windows and lit some sage and played her favorite songs and told her I love you I love you I love you over and over again  

We had just done the hospice intake 24 hours prior but hadn't yet been seen by a nurse. I wished my mom could have gone out more comfortably than she did, but I am choosing to look at the bigger picture, of all of the love and comfort that she experienced over the course of her decline. She spent the last 3 weeks of her life here with me, pretty much bed-bound, and it all happened rather suddenly. She had Alzheimer's and a whole host of other health concerns (it was undiagnosed heart failure that did her in). But at some point in the past week, she had enough presence of mind to say to me: *you have shown me the most love and care of anyone in my life, you are so good to me, thank you for being so good to me* and I know it reveals some serious dysfunction on my part, but it was a privilege for me to be able to nurse my mother in her final days. I love you mommy. I will always love you. 

Thank you from the bottom of my heart to this subreddit. You have been there for me since day 1, and there were times I didn't think I'd outlive my mom due to the sheer stress of caregiving. I appreciate you all, and my heart is with you

Disabled father’s (56) filthy home

I (25F) have been trying to help my dad for the past year or 2. He is living by himself in the house i grew up in on the top of a mountain. The house is absolutely filthy - mold in rooms, on doors. He smokes 24/7 and the walls are weeping nicotine. Cobwebs everywhere. He’s not able to see well, and is physically disabled with chronic pain, so he doesn’t clean up well after the few pets he has left. He has not taken pets to the vet in over a year, and one dog may be put down due to medical neglect & age. In order to enter the house, he has to go up a flight of stairs which he crawls up. He does not eat a good diet, orders shelf stable food on Amazon and takeout - is also diabetic. He refuses to move out of the house. I clean the best I can but every time I go over it’s filthy. He doesn’t shower - the tub is full of cobwebs. He will not move to be closer to me, will not move to even a smaller house that is more maintainable and safe. I don’t know what to do but can not just watch my father rot anymore when nothing I do helps - I’d rather not be involved then, but I feel awful. He has no support. My siblings do not talk to him as he was and is pretty nasty and verbally abusive to say the least. Am I an awful person for no longer enabling or stressing myself out over my stubborn, mean father who is unable to take care of himself, but refuses to compromise with his only source of support? Why am I things and stressing over him being taken care if he is not willing to care for himself in any capacity? (End rant/need for validation/yearning for advice)

Advice needed

My mom (80 yrs) just came to live with me, my husband, and my two little kids about 10 days ago. I'm a stay at home mom. Although she's relatively independent (she can walk, use the toilet, wash herself, etc.) I prepare her meals, started helping her pay bills, appointments, and other little things throughout the day. My mom doesn't need a whole lot of care, like what a home health aide would provide, but I need something to take the edge off of all my duties, aside from the childcare which I prefer to do myself. My mom suggested a cleaning service, but the 5 of us are pretty much always home. We discussed using a send out laundry service and planning to get takeout 2-3 times a week to cut down on the cooking. Thanks for helping me brainstorm other ideas.

Moving mom into a nursing home.

Hello, I haven’t posted for a while, but I was really struggling with what to do about my mother. It finally came to a point a few weeks ago where she admitted she can no longer live alone. I called the nursing home she’d stayed in previously and they were happy to take her back. It was hard, but it had to happen. 

Now she’s getting settled into her new home and well as she can. My new problem is taking care of her apartment. I have to get everything moved out, cleaned, etc. 

It’s an absolute nightmare. I begged her to please not spend all her money on junk. Now there is SO MUCH stuff, and there is just no room for it. I don’t even know what to do with it. The other problem was her incontinence. The smell in there is unbelievable, and I know they’re going to stick me with a huge cleaning bill. My dad was evicted from his place and I got a bill for $2,000. I’m guessing it’ll be the same or more. And again, she blew through her savings ordering stuff off Amazon. So am I going to have to pay this bill? (To be clear, I understand the bill. She ruined their apartment and they’re not happy. But I don’t have any extra money lying around.)

So now I’m trying to pack and clean, but it’s just me doing everything and I am overwhelmed. I am very overwhelmed. Just being over there with the smell is terrible. I’m trying to take it one day/room at a time, but it’s just so much. The carpets have poop matted into them. Nothing touches the smell. I don’t even know what she did to the walls and kitchen floor, but it’s not pretty. 

Any advice is welcome.

Mom's depression/anxiety/health issues taking a toll on me

I’m at my wits’ end! My brother (33) and I (44) recently moved in with our mom (68) to save money and better care for her. I didn’t realize how hard it would be.

She’s the best mom ever, but she struggles with depression, high anxiety, COPD, and other health issues. She hates being home alone, so I’ve missed work to stay with her a few times just so someone is in the house. Even short outings or trips make her anxious. Every morning starts with something negative, and it’s taking a toll on my own mental health (I also deal with depression/anxiety). I’ve noticed myself drinking more just to cope.

We’ve been to the ER multiple times in the last few months. She’ll panic that something is wrong with her heart or stomach, but the tests always come back normal. The real issue is COPD, but she doesn’t want to quit smoking, so she fixates on other possible causes instead. Like she would rather have a heart problem then face the fact that she needs to quit smoking. This morning she was laying in the bed so depressed at the realization that she definitely needs to quit. 

She refuses therapy or medication adjustments because of past bad experiences, but now suddenly says she wants to see a psychiatrist/therapist—mostly, I think, to avoid facing smoking cessation. She has no social life, no hobbies, and little energy. I wish she would "get a life" and find some joy. It's like she's given up.

I feel stuck between wanting to be supportive and just being completely drained. I love her, but I dread walking in the door each day because it’s constant negativity. My brother and I know we’re enabling her, but it’s so hard to watch her suffer. And I don't just mean the smoking, she has other issues as well.

Her mood affect my mood and i'm miserable every day. How can I be supportive to what she's going through and still be able to figure out my own life? I don't want to come off like an A hole to her but its getting to the point where I just kind of avoid her and stay in my room most of the time.

I don’t want to do this again

My (53f) husband (52m) of 29 years has been chronically ill with kidney disease that was diagnosed shortly after we were married.  It was managed with medication, but we knew eventually he would need a transplant. We did a living donor transplant 4 years ago. That kidney has failed and he’s in worse shape than he was before the transplant. This time he’s on dialysis. 
I don’t want to do this again. I don’t want to have to keep track of appointments and make sure he’s taking meds and getting labs drawn.  Our kids are grown (we have 23 year old girl triplets) and I was just getting my own life back. 
Any time I ask him anything he’s angry at me so I’ve just been letting him manage it all, but I know I’m going to be the one that ends up having to check up on everything because he just doesn’t do things. That’s how he deals with things he doesn’t want to face. He just doesn’t do them. 
I feel like the worst person ever, but I just don’t want to do this. It’s just so overwhelming to think of having to deal with this. 

(Yes, I am in therapy…I guess I just want to hear from others that are in similar situations)

tl;dr husband’s transplanted kidney failed, now he’s on dialysis and I don’t want to take care of him again so I feel like a terrible person

How to cope

Hello, I am 18(F), high-school student caring for my mother with PPMS (primary progressive multiple sclerosis) and this is a rant/asking for advice. My mom has been diagnosed \~15years ago but her illness is becoming more difficult to deal with. This year shes almost completely dependent on a wheelchair chair (but can’t move by herself) , having bladder and defecation problems. My parents got divorced three years ago so it’s just me and my mother. She has a caregiver, who is mostly takes care of house chores and shopping (a few days every other week). I am completely overwhelmed, irritated at everything and i feel like i bad person for it and don’t know how to handle these kinds of emotions. I can’t tell my friends about anything so I’m writing it on here. Living like this is hell for me, i want to have my own life and i feel like she isn’t considerate about me at all. I have to make meals, help her with the toilet, help her move in and out of the wheelchair, clean after her… There was recently an incident where she couldn’t hold her bowel movement in and i had to clean it up, i pretended and felt like it was nothing but later i went into my room and just broke down crying. But at times like this i don’t know what exactly I am feeling. There are times when i just cry in the evening because I’m so devastated…

I know she can’t do anything about it and it’s not her fault but I sometimes feel just angry at her. I never snap at her bc i know i would just make it worse. Cherry on top my mom’s also a very naive person and doesn’t want to go outside at all so her personality makes dealing with her even worse. 

This post is not well written but I hope someone can help.. please help

I think it's time.

After an appointment with mother's doctor, I believe it's time to stop her meds with the exception of Metropolol. She was prescribed Clonazapam on an as-needed basis. To me, it seems surreal to give her a benzo but, here we are. This woman truly is over the meds and I need to listen to her, even though the doubts are insurmountable. No choice is a "happy" one. Her appetite has significantly decreased, and I still try and maintain her calories. \*The challenge\*: Keep her on her medicines and have her barely living in misery. Or, begin to taper off the pills and maybe she'll at least not sleep 22 hours a day. My brain is fried, and my body is feeling the weight of this all. Leaving this here in the event anyone else can relate. You're not alone.

How to set boundaries with parents who need lots of help?

My husband works hard so I can be a stay at home mom. With that we try to make the most of his time off and we also don’t live a humble life. We are almost always just getting by with the help of our credit cards.

My parents have made terrible choice after terrible choice and now that they are in their 60s they need lots of help. I have siblings and we try to share the load. Almost every day it’s take this parent here, buy this parents this, let them borrow something, go to this appointment, etc. 

My husband is not on board for. He hates that it cuts into our time and our finances. I always feel in the middle. He has a hard time with my mom because she’s got a lot of mental issues and she’s been rude. And that’s putting it the simplest way. He has expressed how it’s stressful to waste gas that he just filled or if the borrow something and it breaks they won’t be able to buy a new one so he will be stuck paying for it when he’s already working so much. I understand him but when I get the call from my parents saying no makes me feel so guilty. Even though they have problems we’ve always been raised to help family or anyone as much as you can. It’s been eating at me feeling like I have to choose between my family I’ve created and the family I’ve come from. 

Also when I say no I just add to my sibling load. It all just seems really unfair and I’m not sure how I can go about setting boundaries or does that make me selfish? I feel like I’m either selfish for not taking care of my parents or selfish for ignoring how my husband is getting stressed. Any advice would be appreciated. 

* I forgot to add that a lot of what we have to deal with is last minute. A call from my parent that they forgot they have to do this and they need me to take them. Or they forgot they lost their food card and waited until all the food was gone and now they need me to take them to the welfare office before it closes. Lots of last minute things

My brother and his wife financially exploiting my parents?

If anyone has advice or insight, I would be most grateful.

Today my parents confided in me the extent to which my brother and his wife have been making financial demands on them, and how stressful it has become for them.

Some facts for context:

We are not in the US.

My parents are 77yo and retired. They have decent (but not extravagant) assets & income.

I am single, female, under 50yo, no children, and live near my parents.

My brother (over 50yo) and his wife live in a different city.

In the last ten years, my parents have given very generously both to my brother and me: they paid off the mortgage on my modest 1-bedroom flat, and gave me some money for renovations. They paid for my brother's wedding, gave them (my brother and his wife) a 3-bedroom flat in an expensive city, helped them buy a house in another city, paid for expensive renovations, paid for a European holiday, gave them each a year's salary so they could sort themselves out, and continue to pay bills on the home they live in.

I am truly not bothered if they want to spend more money on my brother and his wife! My needs are modest (and are well and truly met). My parents' money is theirs to spend as they please.

**Why?**
